_schema.purpose: Every fixed-point bound this lane has proved, machine-readable, so that code applies the strongest one rather than whichever was current when the file was written.
_schema.why: At pass 59 I opened the order-8 row and used the arithmetic value 26 at orbit size 4, ignoring the 22 this lane had proved one pass earlier -- the exact failure I had diagnosed in another lane at pass 53. A principle in a note did not stop me. A registry that code reads does.

fields.orbit_size: size of the orbit the bound is read off
fields.group: the group induced on the orbit; 'any' if the bound does not depend on it
fields.n: graph order the bound is proved at; 'any' if it holds for every n
fields.bound: maximum number of points the whole group can fix
fields.source: artifact in this directory that proves it
fields.supersedes: a weaker registry entry this one replaces, if any

entries.note: R(3,5)-1 + R(5,4)-1; researcher-1's involution lemma is this with parity, giving 36.
researcher-1's pass-1 value for p = 3, reproduced by the closed form.
The arithmetic bound. Tight as a one-orbit argument: orbit4_exact.py exhibits a (5,5,30)-graph attaining it.
The global count. f = 26, 25, 24 refuted at n = 31, 33, 35 respectively; homogeneous shapes give 19; odd orbits give 22 by the prime-order route.
Z_2^3 and Z_4 x Z_2 regular orbits; the bound depends on the group, not only the size.
